title: Derived representatives for underlying continuous-coefficient Hom
statement: Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and any $k_0$-scheme $X$. Let $\mathcal A$ be the native ordinary continuous-coefficient module category on its geometric fiber [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], and let $T=\operatorname{standardHomModel}(\operatorname{underlyingHomBifunctor})$ [def-sf-standard-bifunctor-hom-model, def-sf-ringed-two-injective-models]. There exist $H:D(\mathcal A)^{\mathrm{op}}\times D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ and $\rho:\operatorname{Representatives}(T.\mathrm{complex},H)$. In particular, for every arbitrary source $K$ and K-injective target $I$, the representative isomorphism $H(QK,QI)\simeq Q T(K,I)$ is natural in both variables, and the prescribed pair of quasi-isomorphisms becomes invertible. No Weil action, native slice normalization or forgetting comparison is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0A95, lemma-RHom-well-defined, and Tag 08J7, section-internal-hom; native product-Hom signs in lean/WeilConjectures/Algebra/Homology/BifunctorHomComplex.lean and native source comparison in lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/BifunctorHom.lean.

proof.text: The underlying category is the module-object category of sheaves over the native coefficient ring. Its sheaf flat-resolution theorem and inheritance by internal modules give a flat separator P. The relative tensor functor with P is exact.

Choose a flat separator P in the ordinary module category. Identify Mod.tensorLeft P with relative tensoring by P using its explicit coequalizer, and transpose maps from P into the native Hom complex into cochains from source tensor P into I. Exactness of this tensor functor preserves acyclicity. K-injectivity makes every cocycle a coboundary, so every map from P to a cycle lifts to the preceding degree. The separator property kills kernel(d) to cokernel(previous d), proving Hom acyclic. Apply the signed source-cone comparison, the quasi-isomorphism/cone criterion, and shift stability to obtain source invariance. For target invariance, lift a target homotopy h to the native Hom complex with p component (-1)^p H(K^p,h). Its homotopy equation follows from target functoriality, source naturality, and cancellation of the two mixed terms. Hence Hom carries a target homotopy equivalence to a homotopy equivalence, and inverts quasi-isomorphisms between K-injectives.

Let I be the canonical functorial K-injective replacement and aug its natural quasi-isomorphism from the identity. By augmentation naturality and two-out-of-three, I preserves quasi-isomorphisms. The two invariance results show that F = (identity.prod I) followed by nativeHomComplex and Q inverts the product quasi-isomorphism class. Set H = Localization.lift F along Q.op.prod Q, and let e be Localization.fac. The natural transformation alpha from nativeHomComplex followed by Q to (Q.op.prod Q) followed by H is Hom(identity,aug) followed by e.inv. On every arbitrary source and K-injective target alpha is invertible by target invariance. Define rho.iso as its inverse. Cancel alpha on the right and use its naturality to prove the simultaneous representative square. Apply source and target invariance directly to prove rho.inverts. The standard model changes only its projections, so its underlying complex functor is exactly nativeHomComplex.
